newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on bearish sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down after breaching a 49-point resistance level on Tuesday on bearish sentiment because of a ban on domestic investors buying B shares, brokers said.
The index shed 0.223 points or 0.45 percent to 48.836 points, on volume of 7.8 million shares worth $3.1 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded, with 19 down, seven flat and eight up.
Brokers said that the market was bearish after the ban, reaffirmed by the government on Saturday, with overseas institutions withdrawing their capital from the market.

"Some domestic institutions can buy B shares through various channels despite the ban but had no interest in building positions as the index is expected to fall further in the coming days," a brokers said.
"The 49-point level has been breached despite institutional support over the past few days and the index will fall further but should find support around 47-48 points," a second broker said.
China Textile Machinery was the biggest loser on speculative selling, plunging $0.030 or 26.78 percent to $0.082, on volume of 4,100 shares.

Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliance followed on bad prospects because of fierce competition in the domestic refrigerator market, falling $0.050 or 11.11 percent to $0.400, on volume of 49,600 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on cross-trading, falling $0.008 or 1.63 percent to $0.480, on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Shanghai A shares closed down on late profit-taking after yesterday's sharp rise, brokers said.
The A index fell 2.114 points or 0.24 percent to 891.441 points, on volume of 727.1 million shares worth 7.2 billion yuan. The SSE 30 edged down 6.504 points or 0.27 percent to 2373.502 points.
Hangzhou Jiefang Road Department Store performed the worst, slipping 0.59 yuan or 6.14 percent to 9.01 yuan, on volume of 2.1 million shares.
